title: What is answer engine optimisation (AEO)?
description: AEO means writing pages so AI assistants and search features can quote a clear, direct answer. Here is how it differs from SEO and how to start.
author: Don
intro:
Search is no longer only a list of links. AI assistants and search features now answer questions directly, quoting the pages that answer them best.

Answer engine optimisation (AEO) is the practice of writing for that: clear questions, direct answers, and structure machines can read.
takeaways:
AEO is about being the quoted answer, not only a ranked link.
Put the direct answer in the first sentence under each question.
Structured data (Article, FAQPage) helps machines understand the page.
Good SEO basics still apply: fast pages, clean URLs, real expertise.
q1: What does answer engine optimisation mean?
a1:
Answer engine optimisation is writing and structuring a page so that AI assistants and search features can lift a clear, accurate answer from it.

Instead of optimising only for a position in a list of links, you optimise to be the source an assistant quotes when someone asks a question.
q2: How is AEO different from SEO?
a2:
SEO aims to rank a page for a search query; AEO aims to have a specific passage chosen as the answer.

They overlap heavily. AEO builds on SEO & adds a stronger focus on question-shaped headings, short self-contained answers and structured data.
q3: How do I start with AEO?
a3:
Start by turning each section heading into the question a reader would actually ask, then answer it in the first one or two sentences.

Add an FAQ for the follow-up questions, mark the page up with Article and FAQPage structured data, and keep each post focused on one topic.
faq_a1: No. AEO builds on SEO. Pages still need to be crawlable, fast and trustworthy before any answer engine will quote them.
faq_q2: Do I need structured data for AEO?
faq_a2: It is not strictly required, but Article and FAQPage markup make the page's meaning explicit, which helps both search engines and AI assistants.
